articles.title: Nvidia pauses server chip shipments to Southeast Asia
articles.summary: Nvidia has instructed its manufacturing partners to temporarily halt server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia. This move comes as the United States intensifies its efforts to restrict the flow of advanced artificial intelligence chips into China.

articles.title: Social network X introduces parental controls after two decades
articles.summary: Elon Musk's social media platform X has finally rolled out parental controls for teenage accounts. This new feature provides parents and guardians with the necessary tools to monitor and manage the content their children view on the application.

articles.title: S&P considers credit downgrade for Nvidia over governance risks
articles.summary: Credit rating agency S&P is evaluating Nvidia for a potential credit downgrade to AA-, which would be its fourth-highest rating. The review is reportedly driven by concerns regarding corporate governance and associated key man risks.

articles.title: FCC approves SpaceX plan for space-based AI data centers
articles.summary: The FCC has approved SpaceX's proposal to place artificial intelligence data centers in space. The agency dismissed opposition concerns regarding threats to scientific research, stating those issues fell outside of its specific regulatory jurisdiction.

articles.title: OpenAI combines Chat and Work with single usage meter
articles.summary: OpenAI announced it is merging the Chat and Work experiences into a unified platform. As part of this integration, heavy ChatGPT users may encounter usage limits sooner due to the implementation of a single, shared usage meter.

articles.title: Tesla Cybertruck becomes America's fastest-selling used truck
articles.summary: Despite being cancelled, the Tesla Cybertruck emerged as the fastest-selling used truck in the United States last month. Used models averaged only 39.1 days on the market, significantly faster than the 65.5-day average for trucks overall.

articles.title: Anthropic CEO dismisses claims of surrendering control to AI
articles.summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has pushed back against rival criticisms accusing him of favoring the surrender of human agency to artificial intelligence. This debate unfolds as leading tech firms increasingly automate their internal research and model development.

articles.title: Password manager 1Password reports internal system breach
articles.summary: Password manager developer 1Password revealed that a hacker gained unauthorized access to an internal employee corporate account, acquiring some customer information. However, the company assured users that their master passwords and vaults remain secure.

articles.title: Android app developers face mandatory public address policy
articles.summary: Independent Android app developers are expressing privacy concerns over a new Google policy requiring many of them to publicly share their physical addresses and phone numbers. The change complies with European Union regulations under the Digital Services Act.

articles.title: Federal judge blocks FCC review of ABC broadcast licenses
articles.summary: A US district judge has issued a preliminary injunction blocking the FCC from conducting an early review of ABC's broadcast licenses. The judge also rejected the agency's motion to dismiss ABC's First Amendment lawsuit alleging retaliation.

articles.title: Rockstar Games developers vote against formal unionization
articles.summary: Workers at Grand Theft Auto VI developer Rockstar Games have voted against formal union recognition, with only 25 percent supporting the agreement. Despite the failed vote, the union stated that organizers will continue their efforts.

articles.title: Ford unveils GT41 prototype to target Le Mans victory
articles.summary: Ford has officially introduced its new GT41 prototype vehicle. The company plans to enter the upcoming World Endurance Championship in 2027 with this machine, aiming to secure another victory at the prestigious Le Mans race.

articles.title: Global warming linked directly to drained peatlands
articles.summary: A detailed historical estimate tracing carbon emissions back to the year 1800 reveals that the draining of peatlands is responsible for a measurable percentage of total global warming by liberating trapped carbon.

articles.title: European spacecraft reveals chaotic aftermath of asteroid collision
articles.summary: Following an asteroid deflection experiment, a European spacecraft observed a surprisingly chaotic and messy scene. Scientists noted that while they knew the DART impact created a massive disruption, the exact nature of the debris was previously unclear.

articles.title: Search alternative Kagi launches privacy-focused Gmail rival
articles.summary: Alternative search engine Kagi has expanded its offerings by launching a new email service designed to rival Gmail. The product's main selling proposition centers on a unique combination of strict privacy promises and integrated artificial intelligence features.

articles.title: Backblaze clarifies data sharing policies with advertisers
articles.summary: Cloud storage provider Backblaze addressed customer concerns by explaining its data sharing practices with advertisers. The company explicitly reassured users that their private backup files and stored personal data will never be shared.

articles.title: FCC authorizes SpaceX to deploy one million satellites
articles.summary: The FCC has officially authorized SpaceX to deploy a massive constellation of one million satellites. If fully realized, this deployment would dramatically increase the total number of artificial satellites currently in orbit by roughly 50-fold.

articles.title: Etsy clarifies artificial intelligence terms after seller backlash
articles.summary: Etsy has revised and clarified its policies regarding the use of artificial intelligence following notable pushback from platform sellers. However, some veteran creators and illustrators dismissed the updated terms as mere sugar coating.

articles.title: Huawei faces steep penalties for stealing US trade secrets
articles.summary: The US Department of Justice stated that Huawei made little effort to conceal its theft of valuable trade secrets from American companies T-Mobile and Cisco. Consequently, Huawei is now facing severe legal penalties and financial liabilities.

articles.title: Backloggd urges users to reset passwords after data breach
articles.summary: Video game tracking platform Backloggd has advised its user base to update their account passwords immediately following a security breach. Affected individuals will need to log back into the service and establish new credentials.
